title: Oracle service run
statement: Let $C$ be a finite-state Boolean machine with $C.k$ work tapes, where $0<C.k$, and let $en$ and $ex$ be states of $C$. Let $\iota$ be an embedding of $1+C.k$ tapes into a host machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $src$ be a host tape distinct from the embedded bank tape indexed by the first virtual bank index. Fix a Boolean input word $x$, a host configuration $d$ in sweep phase whose embedded tapes are all blank and whose embedded tape heads are all at cell $0$, and Boolean words $arg$ and $result$ and a natural number $t$. Suppose that for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |arg|$, the content of $src$ at offset $p$ from its head is the content of the buffer storing $arg$ at cell $p$. If running $C$ from state $en$ with $arg$ on its first work tape and all other work tapes blank reaches the configuration with state $ex$ and $result$ on its first work tape, all other work tapes blank, after $t$ steps, and does not reach state $ex$ at any earlier time, then the composed machine, started from $d$ with its state mapped into the first component of the disjoint union, reaches after $2|arg|+3+t$ steps the configuration obtained by replacing the embedded first bank tape with the buffer storing $result$ and mapping the state into the second component with value $(ex,\mathrm{true})$. At every earlier time $s<2|arg|+3+t$, its state is different from $(ex,\mathrm{true})$ in the second component.
